title: Jesu, We Look to Thee
description: Jesu, We Look to Thee in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 485.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-su, we look to thee, Thy pro-mised pre-sence claim! Thou in the midst of us shalt_ be, As-sem-bled in thy name: Thy name sal-va-tion is, Which here we come to prove; Thy name is life, and health, and peace, And ev-er-last-ing love.

lines: Thou in the midst of us shalt be,
Which here we come to prove;
Thy name is life, and health, and peace,
Not in the name of pride
From nature's paths we turn aside,
We meet, the grace to take
We meet on earth for thy dear sake,
That we may meet in heaven.
Now, Lord, let every bounding heart
And bid our inmost souls rejoice

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
